output.brief: The rise in delayed alarm responses comes from the 12 August move of the alarm relay server, not from agency nurses. The import skipped 11 of 14 forwarding rules. These included the 15-second hold-off for brief SpO2 dips, repeat-alarm suppression, and routing of technical alarms to the charge phone only. Pods A-C therefore get about double the phone notifications per nurse, from about 38 to about 82 per shift, and median acknowledgement time doubled from 34 s to 71 s. Pod D still uses the old server and shows no change. Bedside alarm volume was flat, so acuity and the September monitor update don't explain it. Core, agency and new-graduate nurses are all affected similarly within the affected pods, so this isn't a staff-quality problem. The timing matches the weekly incident step. I'm quite confident. Don't approve the agency cap or the performance reviews. They would punish the wrong people and discourage reporting. Do restore the full rule set, with clinical validation and committee sign-off, and track notifications per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly. Don't switch off SpO2 forwarding to phones. Wireless coverage upgrades aren't justified yet. Sick-leave link to alarm load is plausible but unproven.
